newsitem.title: USA: NYS to start getting sales taxes from some tribes.
newsitem.headline: NYS to start getting sales taxes from some tribes.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki, who earlier said he had agreed interim tax pacts with some Native American tribes, on Monday said Albany would start collecting sales taxes from the other tribes on April 1.

"We're going to move forward with the regulations," he told reporters in Albany, adding the state also would move ahead with talks with four tribes that did not reach preliminary agreements governing cigarette and motor fuel taxes on products sold on their reservations to outsiders.

Pataki added the talks were difficult and that his Administration aimed to reach similar pacts with the other tribes. He earlier said he reached 30-day agreements with the Onondaga, Oneida, Tuscarora, Tonawanda Seneca and Cayuga Indian Nations that will force them to collect motor fuel and cigarette taxes if long-term agreements have not been signed when the pacts end. Talks continue with other tribes: the Seneca, St. Regis Mohawks, the Shinnecock and the Poospatuck.

Under the pact, the five tribes will raise the prices of cigarettes sold on their reservations as a first step in getting "an acceptable level of parity," he said, in prepared remarks. The Oneida also agreed to do the same for gasoline.
The final agreements are expected to include a "specific dollar amount" defining the new prices, Pataki said.

Further, the Onondaga, Tonawanda Seneca, Tuscarora and Cayuga Indian Nations agreed to stop selling motor fuel. They are holding separate talks with the Independent Producers of Petroleum to get tribal pumps at nearby off-reservation stations so that their members can continue to buy the fuel without paying taxes. No estimates on how much new business the convienence stores will get can be made until the final pacts are approved, Pataki said. Initial data had showed Albany was losing $110 million a year in revenues by not collecting the taxes.
